notable_absence.finding: All four server:-scoped xrefs on this page are hardcoded to Server 7.1 ('#7.1@server:learn:security/...'), the same stale version pin found on the sibling certificate-based-authentication.md page in this batch. Current Server extraction in this registry is filed under server/8.0. This is a systematic pattern across the Python SDK's security-adjacent concept pages, not a one-off typo.

cross_component_finding: rbac.md and sdk-user-management-overview.md divide the RBAC topic cleanly and without overlap, though neither page states the division explicitly. rbac.md is purely conceptual: it explains the Server RBAC model itself (users/resources/roles/privileges, the authentication-then-authorization flow) and points outward to four Server doc pages (Authorization, Manage Users and Roles, Roles, Resources Under Access Control) for the concrete catalogue - it contains no API syntax at all. sdk-user-management-overview.md is the mirror image: pure SDK API reference (upsertUser/getUsers/getUser/removeUser method signatures, the UserSettings/Role/User object shapes) with no explanation of what RBAC is or why roles matter - it treats 'role' as an opaque string parameter that 'must correspond to a role supported by Couchbase Server', deferring entirely to rbac.md (implicitly, via no cross-link) for what that means. Java's docs fold both halves into one page (concept-docs/sdk-user-management-overview.md, per the round framing); Python instead gives the RBAC-model half its own dedicated concept-docs/rbac.md page - a real structural difference, not just a content split, since Python's user-management overview page is consequently thinner than what a Java-only reader would expect from a page with the same title.
cross_product_finding: First contact for python-sdk in this registry, and the headline structural asymmetry the round called out: Java's SDK docs tree has no rbac.md at all - Server-RBAC content there lives only inside concept-docs/sdk-user-management-overview.md and its paired howto. Python's docs tree splits this into a dedicated concept-docs/rbac.md (confirmed to exist at python-sdk/current/concept-docs/rbac.md) plus its own sdk-user-management-overview.md, meaning Python documents RBAC as a first-class SDK concept in its own right while Java treats it as a subsection of user management. This is a genuine information-architecture divergence between the two SDKs' doc sets for the same underlying Server feature, not merely a difference in prose. Filed as docs-issues/java-python-sdk-rbac-page-structure-inconsistency at reconciliation (round 30).
